Both tests pass, confirming Lombok's `@Data`/`@NoArgsConstructor`/`@AllArgsConstructor` are correctly generating getters, setters, constructors, and `equals`.

Project is set up at `/home/aman/Desktop/chains/ai-bump/benchmark/top/maven-top-05-lombok/nohook`:

- **`pom.xml`** — Java 17, Lombok 1.18.36 (`provided` scope, wired into `maven-compiler-plugin` as an annotation processor), JUnit 5 for tests.
- **`src/main/java/com/example/model/Person.java`** — `@Data @NoArgsConstructor @AllArgsConstructor` generates all getters/setters/`equals`/`hashCode`/`toString` plus both constructors from three fields, no boilerplate written by hand.
- **`src/main/java/com/example/App.java`** — sample entry point using the generated all-args constructor.
- **`src/test/java/com/example/PersonTest.java`** — verifies the generated accessors/constructors/equality actually work (2/2 passing).

One catch worth flagging: the machine's default JDK is 25, and Lombok 1.18.36 currently crashes on it (`ExceptionInInitializerError: TypeTag :: UNKNOWN` — Lombok's javac-internals patch hasn't caught up to JDK 25 yet). I built and tested against JDK 17 (`~/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.13-zulu`), which matches the project's own `maven.compiler.target`. If you build this with plain `mvn test` day-to-day, set `JAVA_HOME` to a 17 or 21 JDK first, or Lombok annotation processing will fail.
